en.title: Activision's Halo Reboot Rumor Sparks Fierce Fan Debate
en.summary: A whisper of a potential Halo reboot by Activision has ignited a passionate discussion among fans. The rumor suggests a complete lore reset, but is this the shake-up the franchise desperately needs, or a step too far?
en.body:
The Halo universe, a cornerstone of console gaming for over two decades, might be on the cusp of a radical transformation. Recent rumblings, originating from franchise insider **TechnicalHalo**, suggest that **Activision** is eyeing a complete reboot for the series. This rumored approach would discard existing lore to create a "greatest Halo game ever," a bold claim that has understandably sent ripples of division through the dedicated fanbase.

For many, the thought of erasing the saga of **Master Chief** and the intricate universe built by **Bungie** and later **343 Industries** is a hard pill to swallow. The original trilogy and **Bungie**'s subsequent **Halo: Reach** are often held up as the gold standard, with many fans feeling that the narrative threads woven in **Halo 4**, **Halo 5: Guardians**, and **Halo Infinite** have strayed from what made the series iconic. This has led to a sentiment that perhaps a "retcon" of post-**Bungie** entries, preserving the beloved early stories while allowing for new directions, could be a more palatable option than a full-scale reboot.

## The Case for a Fresh Start

However, the argument for a clean slate is not without merit. The **Halo** franchise, now approaching its 30th anniversary, carries a significant amount of lore that can be daunting for newcomers. Some believe that a reboot is precisely the shake-up needed to revitalize a series that, by many accounts, has struggled to recapture the magic of its early days. The recent installments have not consistently met the high expectations set by their predecessors, and a reboot could offer a chance to redefine the core elements of **Halo** for a new generation of players, potentially attracting a broader audience without the baggage of decades of continuity.

## Fan Division and the Path Forward

On platforms like Reddit, the debate rages. "I'm against a full reboot," shared one user, "But if they said the **Bungie** era is canon and everything else going forward is being rebooted, I wouldn't be very upset." Another fan mused, "My only other idea for getting back to a good status quo, short of scorching everything, would be to just do what **Terminator** does all the time and just start from **Halo 3** again." These sentiments highlight a community grappling with the franchise's current trajectory, torn between preserving cherished history and embracing a potentially necessary evolution.

## What's Next

While **Activision**'s plans remain unconfirmed by **Xbox** or **343 Industries**, the speculation alone indicates a strong desire within the community for **Halo**'s future to be addressed. Fans are eager for any official announcements regarding the next steps for the iconic Spartan, and whether that future involves a familiar path or a bold new beginning.

content_raw: Halo fans are divided on whether or not Activision should completely reboot the franchise or keep Master Chief's story going. A rumor floating around the internet from a user named TechnicalHalo suggests that Activision will totally reboot the series, throwing all of the lore out the window in favor of a fresh start. We advise you take this with a grain of salt, as we have no idea what Activision's plans are for Halo, but it has started an interesting conversation among fans. Should Activision use its first Halo game to create a clean slate for the beloved sci-fi franchise? A segment of fans are under the impression that, although Halo has gone off the rails in the last decade, there are still some elements from the newer games that are worth keeping. Bungie's contributions to the franchise (Halo: Campaign Evolved through Halo: Reach) are valued by fans, so some believe that if there's a way to retcon Halo 4 and onwards, that would be a valid option, as well. This ensures that the most beloved Chief stories remain canon, while also giving Activision an option to tell a whole new era of stories in the Halo universe. "I’m against a full reboot," said one fan on Reddit . "But if they said the Bungie era is canon and everything else going forward is being rebooted, I wouldn’t be very upset. Halo 4 has grown on me over the yearsm but 5 and Infinite’s story led nowhere." "My only other idea for getting back to a good status quo, short of scorching everything, would be to just do what Terminator does all the time and just start from Halo 3 again. But it would basically nullify any investment people had in the last decade+, even if it wasn't much, and still give the impression there's no direction if you cop out on a true follow-up," said another . That same fan suggested the idea of a full blown reboot might be born out of necessity, given Master Chief actor Steve Downes is getting older and will inevitably need to be recast if they want to tell new stories with the character. "Steve Downes I just don't think is a long-term option for Chief anymore at his age and a recast is inevitable. You can keep Taylor as Cortana and the Campaign Evolved recasts but a reboot would immediately clear the deck for new versions of the characters and new actors. I'm actually more interested in a full reboot at this point than even a loose Infinite sequel. A full reboot actually sounds like more of a plan," they added. Another fan echoed these sentiments of recasting Chief: "Honestly might be a good call, even if a lot of Halo fans hate the idea," said another fan. "If they’re wanting to grow the franchise again and get new eyes why saddle this fresh beginning with over 20 years of games, comics, and books.
